figures.finding: Antarctica has no law of its own on this: the Antarctic Treaty freezes the territorial claims without settling them, and puts the Treaty's observers and exchanged scientists (and their staffs) under their own country's jurisdiction alone; for everyone else jurisdiction is left unsettled. So a person working in Antarctica carries his own country's rules (those of the expedition's or employer's state, where it applies its law to its nationals there), and no Antarctic rule on the age of majority exists to model.

value.follows: the person's (or employing state's) own law, under Antarctic Treaty art. VIII for observers and scientists; otherwise unsettled

sources.said: 1. Nothing contained in the present Treaty shall be interpreted as: (a) a renunciation by any Contracting Party of previously asserted rights of or claims to territorial sovereignty in Antarctica; … observers designated under paragraph 1 of Article VII and scientific personnel exchanged under subparagraph 1(b) of Article III of the Treaty, and members of the staffs accompanying any such persons, shall be subject only to the jurisdiction of the Contracting Party of which they are nationals in respect of all acts or omissions occurring while they are in Antarctica
